subject: [AMBER] How to cap the residue/ nucleotide atoms

messages.author: Rana Rehan Khalid
messages.body:
Dear amber Users
I have a nucleotide lets consider guanine and I want to cap the basepairing
(G-C) atoms of guanine. And want to study the affect of other 2 atoms on
the protein surface. How can I do this. I actually want, not to allow
basepairing atoms to interact with surface  residue.
Please guide.
Best

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Fri, Aug 13, 2021, Rana Rehan Khalid wrote:
>
>I have a nucleotide lets consider guanine and I want to cap the basepairing
>(G-C) atoms of guanine. And want to study the affect of other 2 atoms on
>the protein surface. How can I do this. I actually want, not to allow
>basepairing atoms to interact with surface  residue.
You'll probably have to think more carefully about what you want to
accomplish.  What (exactly) do you mean when you say that certain atoms
don't "interact" with other atoms or residues?  Are you trying to eliminate
hydrogen bonds between the guanine and the protein?  Or something else?
....dac

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Sat, Aug 28, 2021, Rana Rehan Khalid wrote:
>Yes you are right I actually want to eliminate hydrogen bond of some
>guanine atoms (not all) so that those atoms not interact with protein.
>Kindly guide how can I do this. Thanks
I've got no ideas right now.  You might think about changing the charges on
some of the guanine atoms, so that there is no electrostatic attraction to
potential hydrogen bond partners.  (This would affect all interactions, not
just potential partners on the protein, but also with water or other nucleic
acids.).
Don't be afraid to experiment. But this is definitely not any kind of
standard modification, so you should expect a trial and error experience to
get things to do work they way you want.
Maybe someone on the list has a different idea here.
....dac
